strengths: The paper addresses an important and timely problem: compact autoregressive tokenization for artist-style triangular mesh generation, with attention to topology and connected components.

The proposed layer-based vertex ordering plus self-layer/between-layer adjacency tokenization is conceptually interesting and reasonably well explained, with substantial appendix detail for special cases and non-manifold preprocessing.

Empirical results show consistent, if modest, improvements over reported baselines on CD, HD, NC, |NC|, and face-ratio metrics, and the qualitative figures suggest better preservation of small connected components.
The work discusses practical geometric properties such as manifoldness, normal consistency, and watertight repair, which are valuable for downstream 3D applications beyond visual plausibility.
weaknesses: The central claims about manifold topology, watertightness detection/repair, and connected-component awareness are not evaluated directly with quantitative topology metrics. The paper reports CD/HD/normal metrics, but not rates of manifold meshes, non-manifold edges, boundary holes, watertightness, repair success, or connected-component recall.

The comparison setup is not fully convincing. Only EdgeRunner is explicitly retrained on the same dataset, while it is unclear whether TreeMeshGPT and BPT use comparable training data, model sizes, token budgets, sampling strategies, and conditioning pipelines. This weakens the significance of the small numerical gains over BPT and TreeMeshGPT.

The compression contribution is somewhat overstated. The reported compression ratio matches TreeMeshGPT at 0.22 and improves only from BPT's 0.26, while the method increases vocabulary size and imposes a maximum layer width m that filters data. The derivation relies on approximate average-degree assumptions and does not fully account for extra tokens in special cases.

Ablations are too limited. The only quantitative ablation is the resampling strategy, not the core proposed representation. Missing ablations include connected-component tokens, layer ordering choices, non-manifold preprocessing, window sizes W/W', watertight repair, and the effect of topology tokens versus alternative adjacency encodings.

Several technical claims are insufficiently justified for general meshes. The layer adjacency patterns and normal-orientation constraints appear plausible for many regular triangular surfaces, but edge cases involving boundaries, high genus, irregular valence, disconnected parts, or preprocessing-induced vertex duplication are not rigorously validated.

Reproducibility is limited by a large 500M-parameter model trained for 15 days on 16 H800 GPUs, no apparent code release, incomplete details on baseline training/evaluation parity, and no statistical uncertainty over random seeds or test subsets.

The paper would benefit from clearer positioning against very recent mesh tokenizers and stronger evidence that the method improves user-relevant generation quality rather than primarily improving token accounting and selected reconstruction-style metrics.

Presentation has numerous grammar/terminology issues and occasional imprecision, such as 'vertexes', 'comparation', and unclear statements about planar graph assumptions for processed 3D meshes. These do not prevent understanding but reduce polish for a top-tier submission.

strengths: The paper targets an important and timely problem: compact autoregressive mesh tokenization with better topological validity than local patch methods.

The proposed layered vertex ordering and separate self-layer/between-layer topology tokenization is a coherent idea, and the paper gives reasonably detailed algorithmic descriptions and appendices for the compression scheme.
The method appears to preserve useful mesh-structure constraints, especially manifold-oriented decoding and connected-component markers, which are practically relevant for downstream 3D asset use.

The empirical results show modest improvements over the reported baselines on CD, HD, NC, |NC|, and face-number ratio, and the qualitative examples suggest the method can generate plausible meshes with small connected components.
weaknesses: The empirical evidence is not strong enough for the main claims. The quantitative gains over BPT are very small for CD/HD, and the paper does not provide error bars, confidence intervals, repeated runs, or statistical tests despite claiming clear superiority.

The baseline comparison is weak and potentially unfair. Only EdgeRunner is explicitly retrained on the same data; it is unclear whether TreeMeshGPT and BPT are comparable in training data, model size, conditioning, filtering, and inference settings. DeepMesh is shown only qualitatively.

The evaluation scope is narrow. Although training uses multiple datasets, the main quantitative benchmark uses only 500 gObjaverse meshes, with no per-category breakdown, no evaluation on the other held-out datasets, and no out-of-distribution or robustness analysis.

Key claimed advantages are not directly measured. The paper discusses manifold topology, watertight detection/repair, connected-component awareness, and normal consistency, but lacks direct quantitative metrics such as non-manifold edge rate, watertightness rate, connected-component recall, hole-repair success rate, or invalid-token/decode failure rate.

The novelty over recent mesh tokenization work is incremental. The compression ratio improvement from BPT's 0.26 to 0.22 is modest, and TreeMeshGPT is already reported at 0.22, weakening the central compression claim.

Ablations are insufficient. The only substantive ablation is the resampling strategy, which is borrowed from prior work. There is no ablation isolating the layered ordering, connected-component tokens, self-layer vs between-layer topology tokens, vocabulary/window choices, non-manifold preprocessing, or watertight repair.

The method has nontrivial constraints that may limit generality: it filters meshes with token length above 10000 and layer width above 200, assumes triangular manifold processing, uses a large vocabulary, and may struggle with high-genus or unusual topology. These effects are not empirically analyzed.

The text/image-conditioned results are not compelling as scientific evidence because they rely on external systems to produce dense meshes and then use sampled point clouds as input; this does not demonstrate native text-to-mesh or image-to-mesh capability.

Reproducibility is limited. The paper states that code/checkpoints/data preparation will be released later, but the submitted manuscript does not provide enough concrete release artifacts, exact commands, or baseline reproduction details to verify the main results.

The writing and presentation contain many grammar issues, typos, and imprecise claims, which make parts of the method and evaluation harder to assess. Some checklist answers also appear overstated, especially regarding statistical significance.

strengths: The paper proposes a clear and interesting mesh tokenization scheme based on vertex layering and compressed self-/between-layer adjacency matrices, targeting an important bottleneck in autoregressive mesh generation: long and redundant token sequences.

The method is well motivated by concrete limitations of prior tree-traversal and local-patch tokenizations, especially repeated vertex encoding, component awareness, manifoldness, and normal consistency.

The representation has attractive geometric structure: connected-component tokens, manifold-oriented preprocessing, deterministic layer ordering, and decoding constraints that plausibly improve face normal consistency and support some watertightness detection/repair.

Empirical results are encouraging: the method improves over reported baselines on CD, HD, NC, |NC|, and face-ratio metrics in the main table, while matching the best reported compression ratio and improving over BPT's compression.
The appendix provides useful algorithmic detail for non-manifold processing, matrix compression, compression-ratio reasoning, and training details, making the core idea relatively understandable.
weaknesses: The evaluation is somewhat narrow for a top-tier acceptance: the main quantitative comparison uses only 500 gObjaverse meshes, despite training on multiple datasets, and there is little evidence of generalization across ShapeNet, 3D-FUTURE, Toys4K, or out-of-domain assets.

Several central geometric claims are not directly quantified. The paper emphasizes manifold topology, watertight detection/repair, small connected components, and normal consistency, but does not report manifoldness rates, watertightness rates, repair success rates, connected-component recall, or failure cases.

Baseline fairness is not fully convincing. EdgeRunner is retrained, but it is unclear whether TreeMeshGPT and BPT are reproduced under identical data/model/compute settings; DeepMesh appears only in qualitative comparison, not the main quantitative table.

The numerical gains over the strongest baselines are modest for geometry metrics, and the compression ratio is tied with TreeMeshGPT rather than clearly better than all peers. The paper's framing sometimes overstates the degree of state-of-the-art improvement.

Ablations are limited. The only main ablation concerns progressive balanced sampling, which is not the central tokenization novelty. There are no focused ablations for connected-component tokens, self-layer versus between-layer encoding, start-edge selection, matrix window sizes, vocabulary size, non-manifold preprocessing, or watertight repair.

The compression-ratio analysis relies on approximate assumptions about average mesh degree and token accounting; it does not fully discuss cases with high genus, boundaries, many connected components, large layer width, or extra tokens from out-of-window connections.

Reproducibility is incomplete at submission time: code/checkpoints/data preparation are described as future releases, and some experimental details needed for exact reproduction and baseline comparison remain underspecified.
The writing is understandable but contains many typos and imprecise terms, and some figures/tables carry much of the argument without enough rigorous quantitative backing.

strengths: The paper proposes a concrete and interesting mesh tokenization scheme based on vertex layering plus layer adjacency matrices, targeting important practical properties that are often neglected in autoregressive mesh generation.

The method is well motivated for part-aware and topology-aware generation, and the paper gives a fairly detailed algorithmic description, including appendices with pseudocode, complexity discussion, compression details, and failure cases.

Compression efficiency is a clear positive point: the reported bits-per-face and compression ratio are competitive with recent mesh-tokenization baselines, and the authors make a reasonable effort to avoid evaluating compression only by token count.
The empirical results show promising improvements over selected baselines on CD, HD, normal consistency, and qualitative preservation of small connected components.

The online non-manifold processing and progressive resampling strategy address a real data-scaling issue for mesh generation, and the ablations suggest these choices improve downstream generation quality.
weaknesses: The strongest claims about guaranteed manifoldness, watertightness repair, face-normal consistency, and part awareness are not supported by sufficiently rigorous quantitative evaluation. The paper mostly argues from construction and qualitative examples, but does not report rates of manifold violations, holes, flipped normals, connected-component correctness, repair success/failure, or invalid-token behavior across generated samples.

The evaluation is relatively narrow for a top-tier submission. The main quantitative comparison uses only 500 gObjaverse meshes, and several important recent methods are omitted or only qualitatively compared. DeepMesh is excluded from quantitative results, MeshAnything v2/Nautilus are not empirically evaluated, and BPT/TreeMeshGPT training/evaluation parity is not fully clear.

Some comparisons appear potentially unfair or under-specified. EdgeRunner is retrained on the same dataset with the authors’ resampling strategy, while other baselines may not be retrained under matched data/model/compute conditions. The benefits of the tokenization are therefore somewhat confounded with training data, sampling strategy, and model scale.

The non-manifold processing ablation compares training on all data versus manifold-only data, which demonstrates the value of more data but does not isolate the proposed processing algorithm against alternatives such as libigl or simpler repair pipelines with matched data size. The qualitative comparison to naive processing is not enough to establish the claimed advantage.

The watertight detection/repair argument seems oversimplified: the paper assumes holes correspond to matrix entries predicted as 0 instead of 1 and can be corrected directly, but autoregressive generation can produce many other inconsistent token patterns. The method’s robustness to such errors is not convincingly evaluated.

The method has practical limitations that weaken the claimed generality: meshes with token length above 10k or layer width above 200 are filtered, vocabulary size is large, generation is limited by sequence length, and fine details are degraded by 7-bit quantization.

Reproducibility is limited. The model is large and costly to train, implementation details are incomplete for independently reproducing the tokenizer/decoder/repair procedure, and there is no indication of released code, trained checkpoints, or exact dataset splits.

The paper’s significance is promising but not yet fully established: the contribution is technically plausible and relevant, but the evidence does not yet convincingly demonstrate robust topology preservation and practical superiority across diverse mesh-generation settings.

strengths: The paper targets an important practical weakness of autoregressive mesh generation: preserving topology-related properties such as manifoldness, normal consistency, watertightness, and connected-component awareness.
The proposed layer-wise vertex ordering and adjacency-matrix tokenization is a concrete and potentially useful alternative to treating meshes as unordered triangle collections.
The paper includes several implementation details, pseudocode, complexity discussion, and ablations for resampling and non-manifold processing.
The reported geometric metrics are slightly better than the selected baselines, and the compression analysis attempts to account for vocabulary size through bits-per-face.
weaknesses: The central topology claims are not convincingly validated. The paper repeatedly claims manifoldness, watertight detection/repair, normal consistency, and part awareness, but provides little quantitative evaluation of these properties on generated meshes. There are no reported rates of non-manifold edges, holes, disconnected/mis-partitioned components, repair success, or failure rates.

Several claimed guarantees are insufficiently justified. The argument that layer-wise decoding strictly preserves manifold topology and can repair watertightness appears informal and may not cover arbitrary predicted token errors, high-genus surfaces, boundaries, repeated vertices, or invalid adjacency patterns produced by the autoregressive model.

The experimental comparison is weak for a top-tier venue. Quantitative results are on only 500 reserved gObjaverse meshes, omit several closely related methods from quantitative comparison, and only retrain one baseline under the same data setting. This makes the reported advantage difficult to attribute to the tokenization method itself.

The paper’s positioning is overstated. Table 1 presents broad binary advantages over recent baselines without enough evidence or nuanced discussion, and the text claims state-of-the-art compression and practical geometric integrity more strongly than the experiments support.

Ablations are incomplete. There is no direct ablation of the key tokenization design choices beyond window-size statistics, no evaluation of the watertight repair mechanism, no analysis of invalid token sequences, and limited study of sensitivity to quantization, vocabulary size, max layer width, max sequence length, or topology complexity.

The compression evaluation is not fully persuasive. The compression ratio derivation relies on approximate assumptions about average vertex degree and regular triangular meshes, while real datasets and different topology classes may violate these assumptions. The comparison also standardizes settings in ways that may not reflect each method’s intended operating point.

The non-manifold processing contribution is only weakly evaluated. The paper compares training with more versus less data, but does not isolate the proposed processing algorithm against established mesh repair tools with quantitative measures of surface preservation, fragmentation, or downstream generation quality.

The method has practical limitations that are important but underexplored: a large vocabulary, a 10K token generation cap, filtering by maximum vertices per layer, degraded fine detail at 7-bit quantization, and possible failures on complex geometries.

Presentation quality is uneven. Some mathematical explanations are informal, several claims are asserted rather than proved, and the evaluation narrative often relies on qualitative figures rather than rigorous evidence.

strengths: The paper proposes a clear and useful topology-aware mesh tokenization scheme based on vertex layering, ordered layer traversal, and compressed self-/between-layer adjacency matrices. The representation is well motivated by practical mesh requirements rather than only visual fidelity.

The work targets important limitations of recent autoregressive mesh generators: manifoldness, watertightness detection, normal consistency, and connected-component or part awareness. These are meaningful for downstream editing, simulation, 3D printing, and asset pipelines.

Compression efficiency is a notable strength. The paper reports favorable compression ratio and bits-per-face compared with BPT, EdgeRunner, and TreeMeshGPT, and the appendix gives useful derivations and statistics about vocabulary/window choices.

The empirical results are generally convincing: the method achieves the best reported CD/HD/NC/|NC| among the included baselines, with qualitative comparisons showing improved component awareness and fewer non-manifold artifacts.

The paper includes several practical contributions beyond tokenization, including online non-manifold processing and progressive resampling. The ablations indicate that these design choices improve generation quality and training data scalability.
The manuscript is mostly clear, with good visual explanations of the tokenization process, non-manifold processing, and failure cases.
weaknesses: Some central topology claims are stated more strongly than they are proven. The manuscript argues that manifold topology and face-normal consistency follow from construction, but the exact assumptions and failure modes under autoregressive prediction errors, decoding corrections, unusual genus, boundaries, or invalid token sequences are not formalized enough for the strength of the claims.

The watertightness result is framed as detection and repair rather than strict generation-time guarantee. The repair procedure may change intended geometry or topology, and the paper does not quantify repair frequency, repair accuracy, or cases where repair is ambiguous or harmful.

The quantitative evaluation is somewhat narrow. The main benchmark uses 500 gObjaverse meshes, and only EdgeRunner is explicitly retrained on the same data; comparisons to BPT/TreeMeshGPT/DeepMesh may be affected by dataset, implementation, architecture, and training differences.

The reported gains in generation quality over BPT are positive but modest, while the architecture and training budget are large. The paper would be stronger with significance estimates, broader held-out datasets, and controlled comparisons under identical model capacity and data.

The practical utility claims would benefit from downstream validation, e.g. measuring actual success in editing, rigging, 3D printing, physics simulation, or mesh repair pipelines rather than relying mainly on proxy topology metrics and qualitative examples.

Reproducibility details are incomplete for a top-tier submission: the paper gives many implementation details, but it is unclear whether code, processed data, trained models, exact baseline settings, and evaluation scripts will be released. The 16 H800 / 15 day training cost also raises a barrier to reproduction.

The method has important constraints: token length is capped at 10K, quantization is 7-bit, vocabulary is larger than several baselines, and meshes exceeding layer-size thresholds are discarded. These limitations are acknowledged, but their impact on real-world asset distributions is only partially characterized.
